title: Fine-grained reply-latency SLI mesh and staged multi-region fallback dashboard
creator: Anika Patel
description: Problem: Current SLO telemetry is coarse-grained (route-level p95/p99) and does not capture fine variations caused by sequence-length, KV-cache hits, or ephemeral per-customer throttles during regional incidents. We need an instrumentation and dashboarding effort to: 1) define a fine-grained "reply-latency" SLI (sub-token-aware request-level latency histogram that attributes decode vs. encode vs. kernel time), 2) aggregate those SLIs into a mesh that supports per-region and cross-region SLOs, and 3) build an operational dashboard that surfaces staged circuit states (healthy / warning / shed), automated escalation signals, and guided remediation playbooks.
background: Related initiatives: multi-region failover policies, adaptive load-shedding, and existing failover dashboards. This ticket focuses on instrumentation & visual ergonomics needed for runbook-driven operations. Prior art: earlier token-latency dashboards provided a good starting point but aggregated too aggressively and lacked a clear mapping from low-level metrics to circuit escalation thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Define and document the reply-latency SLI (histogram buckets, tags: region, route, model_variant, seq_len_bucket, kv_hit) in the observability handbook
Servers emit new lightweight metrics at request boundary: reply.decode_ms, reply.kernel_ms, reply.total_ms, reply.token_count with tags attached
Ingestion pipeline supports 1-minute rollups and 1-hour histogram retention for derived SLOs; raw high-cardinality events are sampled at 1% by default and 10% during incidents
Dashboard includes: region overview panel, model-variant cohort breakdown, staged-circuit state timeline, automated escalation hints, and per-customer impact estimate using quota/cost maps
Playbook links (canary rollback, regional evacuate, model-variant fallback) are embedded in dashboard actions
Load test: synthetic probe demonstrates correct SLI derivation and triggers staged-shed states in a canary region
Docs + runbook reviewed by SRE and Product and approved for staging rollout
implementation_notes: Instrumentation: add a small histogram library call in the runtime request pipeline at the end of decode loop to emit decode and kernel contributions. Prefer Envoy metrics for ingress timing, and eBPF for low-overhead kernel timing if available. Use tags to keep cardinality bounded: region, route, model_family, seq_len_bucket (0-64,65-256,257-1024,>1024), kv_hit (true/false). Storage: create derived histograms in metrics cluster with 1m granularity and store 30d for SLO computation. Sampling: implement deterministic sampling by trace_id to allow event replay for sampled traces. Cost estimate: ~120k extra ingested metrics/month at 1% sample; budget impact ~ $3k/month in metric storage. Backwards compatibility: metric names should be prefixed with "rply." to avoid collision with older token metrics.
tradeoffs_and_decisions:
- Granularity vs cost: we chose histogram buckets + sampling instead of full raw traces to balance cost.
- eBPF vs runtime timers: eBPF provides more precise kernel time but adds rollout complexity; plan phased approach: runtime timers first, eBPF as opt-in.
- SLO window: use 30d rolling with 7d burn rate alerts to align with product SLAs.
- Circuit semantics: staged states (ok, warn, shed-soft, shed-hard) to allow progressive mitigation before full failover.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: metric explosion due to high cardinality. Mitigation: enforced tag whitelist and seq_len_bucket coarsening.
Risk: dashboards overloaded with false positives. Mitigation: require multi-signal confirmation (latency + error-rate + capacity) before automated escalations are suggested.
Risk: sampling hides rare degradations. Mitigation: increase sampling during incidents and capture synthetic probes at full fidelity.
rollout_plan: 1) Instrument runtime in staging with 1% sample, validate histograms (Week 1). 2) Build dashboard panels in Grafana using derived histograms; add links to runbook (Week 2). 3) Run synthetic assault (latency/kern heavy) in staging to test staged-shed automation (Week 3). 4) Canary to US-WEST with limited traffic (5% traffic, Week 4). 5) Full rollout with SRE oncall watch (Week 5).
dashboards: Region Overview: aggregated reply.total_ms p50/p95/p99 heatmap by region and model_family
Staged Circuit Timeline: per-region state transitions with correlated admission rate and error budget burn
Cohort Explorer: seq_len_bucket x kv_hit breakdown for p99 latency and kernel contribution
Escalation Panel: suggested next actions (shift traffic, increase kv-cache allocation, fall back to model-quantized variant) with estimated customer impact
Synthetic Probe Monitor: probe success rate, synthetic p99 over time, and differential between probe and real traffic
